scope: Published or reproducible network-behavior fingerprints only. The library is for attribution-resistant defensive measurement and does not contain bypass/exploitation instructions.

primary_measurement_families.name: IN_PATH_DISTRIBUTED_TSPU
primary_measurement_families.evidence: Censored Planet IMC 2022 remotely fingerprinted a centrally controlled but geographically distributed in-path censorship system across more than six thousand observed TSPU devices and roughly 650 Russian ASes.
primary_measurement_families.defensive_use: Treat censorship that localizes close to access networks and repeats a known TSPU response family as stronger evidence than generic timeout observations.
primary_measurement_families.claim_limit: Topology similarity is not device identity.

primary_measurement_families.name: SNI_DEPENDENT_TLS_BLOCKING
primary_measurement_families.evidence: Published TSPU research shows filtering decisions can depend on TLS SNI and can exhibit multiple blocking behaviors rather than one universal reset signature.
primary_measurement_families.defensive_use: Matched destinations/SNI controls help distinguish domain-sensitive policy from endpoint failure.
primary_measurement_families.claim_limit: SNI filtering is common to many DPI systems and is not TSPU-specific by itself.

primary_measurement_families.name: IP_TRIGGERED_FILTERING
primary_measurement_families.evidence: IMC 2022 measurements identified IP-address-triggered TSPU blocking behavior alongside hostname/SNI mechanisms.
primary_measurement_families.defensive_use: Compare name-based and direct-address reachability to separate DNS effects from IP policy.
primary_measurement_families.claim_limit: IP blocking is generic censorship behavior.

primary_measurement_families.name: QUIC_POLICY_AND_SNI_FILTERING
primary_measurement_families.evidence: FOCI 2026 documents Russia moving from broad international QUIC blocking to large-scale SNI-dependent QUIC censorship, demonstrating protocol-specific and rapidly reconfigurable policy.
primary_measurement_families.defensive_use: Use paired TCP/TLS versus QUIC observations to detect protocol-selective intervention rather than generic service unavailability.
primary_measurement_families.claim_limit: QUIC blocking alone does not identify TSPU.

primary_measurement_families.name: ORIGIN_DIRECTION_ASYMMETRY
primary_measurement_families.evidence: FOCI 2026 measurements found the studied Russian QUIC censorship regime affected traffic originating in Russia and leaving the country while measured inbound traffic was not affected in the same way.
primary_measurement_families.defensive_use: Directionality is a discriminator when comparing suspected foreign deployments with known Russian policy families.
primary_measurement_families.claim_limit: Policy can change over time and different TSPU rules may have different directionality.

primary_measurement_families.name: DNS_DESTINATION_INTERCEPTION_CANDIDATE
primary_measurement_families.evidence: Public Russian network experiments beginning around 2026-08-26 reported selective interception/redirection of plaintext UDP DNS requests addressed to public resolvers such as 8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1 while protocol-dependent controls behaved differently.
primary_measurement_families.defensive_use: Candidate early-warning fingerprint only when destination, TTL/path localization and matched TCP/encrypted-DNS controls are captured.
primary_measurement_families.claim_limit: Do not use as sole attribution evidence.

primary_measurement_families.name: FRAGMENTATION_RESPONSE_BEHAVIOR
primary_measurement_families.evidence: IMC 2022 used response differences to packet fragmentation and protocol construction as part of remote TSPU fingerprinting.
primary_measurement_families.defensive_use: Published response ambiguity can help distinguish specific DPI implementation families in controlled measurements.
primary_measurement_families.claim_limit: Must remain within benign measurement traffic and independent replication.

adjacent_research.title: Fingerprinting Deep Packet Inspection Devices by Their Ambiguities
adjacent_research.relevance: Develops remote behavioral fingerprinting of DPI implementations through ambiguity handling; useful methodology for distinguishing commercial/nation-state DPI families without physical device access.

adjacent_research.title: Understanding Routing-Induced Censorship Changes Globally
adjacent_research.relevance: Shows observed censorship can change with routing/ECMP alone, so suspected TSPU fingerprints require stable route capture and matched path controls.

minimum_measurement_bundle: AS path/traceroute or equivalent path evidence
DNS resolver destination and observed response path where relevant
paired TCP/TLS and QUIC reachability where safe and applicable
repeat observation from an independent vantage or platform
attribution_rule: No single timeout, reset, blocked domain, vendor name, or protocol anomaly is a TSPU fingerprint. Escalation requires a composite behavior pattern plus path localization and independent replication.
safety_boundary: Observation and defensive characterization only; no exploitation, unauthorized access, destructive testing, credential use, or evasion deployment.
